question.text: A buyback as an exit mechanism means:

answer.text: The investee company or its promoters repurchase the AIF's shares under a put option, at a price specified by formula or agreement
The fund manager buys back the fund

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook (pp.218-219) describes buyback as an exit route in which the AIF exercises a put option on the shares it holds in the investee company. The repurchase can be effected either by the investee company itself or by its promoters, and the put price is determined by a formula or the terms agreed in the investment documentation. The Trap: A buyback in this exit context is not the AIF acquiring more shares, nor is it the manager buying out the fund, nor anything to do with SEBI buying registrations. It is the predefined contractual right of the AIF to sell back its shares to the company or promoters. Note: Source reference: NISM Series XIX-A workbook pp.218-219 (buyback exit via put option on shares; company or promoter repurchase; put price by formula or agreement).
